title: Ring Count, Skipped
statement: I took Mara Vey's stump and let the clock skip. Below the cut the rings still go round the way years used to; above it they come out straight, like a record that stopped being a record and became a barcode. The last few years do not even stay inside the wood: they run off the edge of the picture, offset by the same thirty-seven pixels my houses slipped by. The heart of the tree is now a small pink square, which is not a thing trees have. The seedling moved to the middle, where the cut is. Someone can decide whether it is growing out of the wound or into it.
process: Kept the stump outline, the roots and the ring spacing from the parent; replaced the upper half of every ring with a straight line at the same height, offset the newest lines sideways, and put one pink square where the pith was.
